title: Karl Lagerfeld's birth chart
metaDescription: Karl Lagerfeld's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.3° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a sextile: Mars and Neptune within 0.2°, drive wired to imagination. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 17.3° Virgo — the second decan, 10°–20°, which the tradition sub-rules by Saturn. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Virgo and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Virgo (15.9°), Venus in Libra (23.9°), Mars in Scorpio (10.0°): a mind that trusts the measured and the checked, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that moves on certainty and current.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Mars to Neptune, a sextile with 0.2° of slack. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Venus square Pluto at 0.5°, and Mars square Saturn at 0.7° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Venus opposes Uranus while both square Pluto. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mercury in Virgo at 15.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Libra at 23.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Scorpio at 10.0° is in domicile; Saturn in Aquarius at 10.7° is in domicile. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 3 earth, 2 air, 2 water, 1 fire by element and 3 mutable, 3 cardinal, 2 fixed by mode. An earth emphasis reads as patience with material reality — slow hands, durable results. Jupiter crossed from Virgo into Libra during that day, so its sign is left open. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.0° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
